body: [{"streamId":"01a0baa9-5718-714f-880d-d28ca56cf16e","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0baa9-5718-714f-880d-d28ca56cf16e\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022An established node can pull a named task\\u0027s event stream, or a project\\u0027s history since a point, from a peer on demand, so work published on one node before replication switched on can be handed to another node that already has its own history\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k task pull \\u003Cid\\u003E (working name; match the noun-first CLI conventions) on a node that lacks that task\\u0027s stream writes a targeted catch-up request naming the stream to the ranked candidate peers through the existing EventCatchUpCoordinator, and the answering peer\\u0027s sweep serves that stream in full through the same envelopes the bootstrap answer uses; the task appears on the requesting node\\u0027s board with its dependencies, stacking, and issue link intact, and the command prints where it stands and what to run next\u0022,\u0022h9k project pull \\u003Cproject\\u003E --since \\u003Cglobal-sequence|all\\u003E requests the project\\u0027s history the same way for a node that has its own history and therefore never bootstraps (MessageSweepEngine.HasAnyLocalHistoryAsync gates the bootstrap to brand-new nodes); an answer is applied idempotently against streams the node already holds\u0022,\u0022The --from-issue refusal for a task published elsewhere names the pull command instead of promising that catch-up will bring the stream, which is true only for a brand-new node; the docs (concepts.md, cli.md) say which node states bootstrap, which gap-fill, and which need a pull\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover: a targeted request for one stream is written and answered; an established node\\u0027s request for history since a point; idempotent application over a stream already held; the refusal text; no test creates branches or touches GitHub\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test pass; the decision log carries one entry under this task\\u0027s placeholder\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Cut 2026-09-19 13:2x EDT on Brian\\u0027s word after the first two-node connection (Mac genesis, Windows joined by invite 12:51 EDT on v0.10.0). Evidence: live replication works (the Mac\\u0027s refs/hall9k/messages/\\u003Cnode\\u003E outbox carries kind=events envelopes with run events after replication_switched_on; the Mac holds an EventReplicationInboxCursor for the Windows node), but the five persona tasks published on the Mac on 2026-09-17 (ec35ceca, cd722750, b1b20c23, 0569c229, 09fad63d) never reach Windows: Windows\\u0027s h9k task add --from-issue 447 answered \\u0027already published elsewhere as task ec35ceca, but that task\\u0027s own event stream has not reached this node yet ... It will appear on this node\\u0027s own board once catch-up brings that stream in\\u0027, while src/Hall9k.Daemon/Messaging/MessageSweepEngine.cs AdvanceCatchUpAsync requests the bootstrap (EventCatchUpCoordinator.RequestBootstrapAsync) only when HasAnyLocalHistoryAsync is false for the project (no ReplicatedEventRecord, no TaskListItem, no IdeaDetails), and RequestGapFillAsync covers outbox seq gaps, not streams that predate the switch-on sequence (ReplicationSwitchedOn.SwitchOnGlobalSequence). Windows has its own hall9k history, so it never bootstraps. Lineage: a gap in M2b (idea 202383dc), not a fix of a fix. Boundaries: reuse EventCatchUpCoordinator, the ranked candidates, the timeout and cascade; do not widen bootstrap to established nodes wholesale; a pull never overwrites a stream the node already holds.
